label: Orchestra Hit, the GS capital tone, read out of a module's own recordings
audition_title: libsonare orchestra hit vs the module's own recordings
_notes: The grid is the library capture's own, every sixth semitone from 48 to 72, so the machine and the modern recording are read over the same register. The source holds a recording at each of these notes.
_velocities: One, and 100 is a label rather than a measurement: the font records no velocity and the importer refuses a grid asking for more than one layer. `vel_range` and the dynamics it feeds are excused in `dimensions_na` for that reason.
_dry: Nothing played this, so nothing was switched off. What the file holds is the module's own PCM with no effect in front of it, which is what `source_class: module` asks for.
_stimulus: The gate is the longest recording of the grid, 1140 ms at note 48, and each note's window ends where its own recording does: 1105, 926, 817 and 680 ms for the others. Nothing pads a recording.
_realtime: Read rather than played: `import_sf2.py` extracts the recorded frames, so there is no host to settle and no lead-in to strip. `preroll_ms` is 0 because a recording begins at its own first frame.
_timbres: One. The source holds exactly one recording per note of this tone, so there is no second of it to disagree with and this capture cannot move the voice past `voiced` however complete its coverage.
_dimensions: Coverage is read against `toneclass.canonical_dimensions`, which for program 55 is 16 dimensions. The four below are what this source cannot carry, each argued from what the font sets rather than from its being a font. Dimensions it can carry are gated.

dimensions_na.vel_range: the font declares no velocity layers at all, so it holds one recording per note at a velocity it does not state. A grid asking for more than one would write that recording into every row of the axis a dynamics fit reads
dimensions_na.stereo: the recordings are mono (one channel) and no pan is read from them, so the image is absent by construction rather than by voicing
dimensions_na.register: the font sets no attenuation per note that this capture reads, so the level relation between one note and the next is the headroom each recording was normalised into rather than the instrument's fall across its compass
dimensions_na.damper: a recording ends where it was cut and carries no note-off, so there is no key lift for a release to be read from
dimensions_na.attack_hf_swing: this reference holds one velocity (100) per note, so there is no softest-to-hardest change to measure -- the same fact vel_range is excused for

_room: The module is recorded with reverb, chorus, delay and the insertion effect all off, and `import_sf2.py --report` plus its own dryness check measure the imported corpus rather than taking this declaration's word for it.
_identity: Which file and which of its presets answered this timbre lives in the untracked sibling `orchestra_hit_module.local.json`. Everything here is the method; scoring, fitting and diagnosing read `reference/orchestra_hit_module.json`.
